title: Follow-up: parseDiff must unquote C-quoted git paths
description: Pre-existing LOW found in the approved review of opum-ai/glyph-cli#34. `git diff` C-quotes non-ASCII and backslash or control-character paths by default (core.quotePath), so the `---`/`+++` lines carry quoted and escaped paths and symbols in such files drop out of `diff`. Fix by unquoting git's path form or by asking git not to quote. Filed from the #34 approval; not started.

acceptanceCriteria.text: parseDiff returns the real path for a non-ASCII file name and for a file name containing a backslash or control character under the default core.quotePath.
A test commits a non-ASCII-named source file and asserts diff reports its symbols.
Existing diff answers are unchanged and `bun run check` passes.

plan: Add a git C-style path unquoter to src/git.ts and apply it to the diff header new-side path, keeping the default core.quotePath.
Unit-test parseDiff against non-ASCII, backslash and control-character paths; an end-to-end diff test over a non-ASCII file asserts its symbols are reported.
Run bun run check and keep every existing diff answer unchanged.
implementationNotes: Proof: CI run 44019198377 on bd15c53 (Check, Docs, Tracker integrity green); bun run check locally green, 76 tests. Mutation check: reverting the two unquoteGitPath calls leaves the other 23 tests in git.test.ts and cli.test.ts green and turns exactly the two new ones red (unit: quoted headers returned verbatim; CLI: symbols empty, filesChanged 0). The parser decodes the C escapes git emits (named ones plus octal bytes), decodes the bytes as UTF-8, then strips the b/ prefix.

DEC-183 reviewer verdict on opum-ai/glyph-cli#62 at head c385ba7a71e1babac1412275b8944c7c685cd915, reviewer model claude-opus-5-5 (read-only unit, no shell, ran nothing). Recorded verbatim:

VERDICT: APPROVE

Review of opum-ai/glyph-cli#62 (GCLI-14) at head c385ba7 by a DEC-183 reviewer unit (claude-opus-5-5): it is read-only, has no shell, and ran nothing.

Findings
1. NIT, test/cli.test.ts:118 (and the mutation claim in .quest/completed/GCLI-14.json). The CLI test exercises only `café`. Scratch repos inherit the caller's environment and global git config: gitRun passes `{...process.env}` at src/git.ts:22, and makeScratchRepo sets only user.email and user.name at test/helpers.ts:28-29. Under a global `core.quotePath=false`, git writes `café` raw, so this test would pass with the fix reverted. The record's claim that "exactly the two new ones" go red therefore holds only under default config. The git.test.ts:30 test stays a real control either way, because git quotes backslash and tab regardless of quotePath. Fix: add `gitRun(root, ["config", "core.quotePath", "true"])` in helpers.ts:28-29, or set GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null in tests.
2. NIT, test/git.test.ts:30. unquoteGitPath (src/git.ts:179) is exported but has no direct unit test on literal strings. Untested: a path that contains a double quote (`"b/a\"b.ts"` → `b/a"b.ts`), the named escapes other than \t and \\, and both fall-back returns (an unknown escape like `\q` at src/git.ts:208, and a trailing lone backslash at :195). A literal-string test such as `unquoteGitPath('"b/caf\\303\\251.ts"')` would also pin the octal path whatever the environment's config.
3. NIT, src/git.ts:212. `new TextDecoder()` is non-fatal, so a non-UTF-8 byte sequence (for example a Latin-1 name) silently becomes U+FFFD. That is quiet corruption, which the docstring at :175-177 says the function avoids. `new TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true })` in a try that returns `path` on failure would match the docstring. Low impact.
4. NIT, pre-existing and not introduced here, src/git.ts:244/248/249. With -U0, a removed content line beginning `-- ` or an added one beginning `++ ` renders as `--- `/`+++ ` and is parsed as a file header. Also, `.trim()` drops real trailing whitespace from an unquoted filename (git does not quote spaces). Worth a separate follow-up; out of scope for GCLI-14.

Verified, by reading the diff, src/git.ts, test/git.test.ts, test/cli.test.ts, test/helpers.ts and the GCLI-14 record:
- Octal escapes: the loop at src/git.ts:202-207 reads at most 3 digits, and each `\NNN` pushes one byte (`& 0xff`). Literal characters are UTF-8-encoded into the same byte array, and the whole array is decoded once with TextDecoder (:212), not char by char. So `\303\251` comes out as é; char-by-char decoding would have given "Ã©". Surrogate pairs are handled through codePointAt and literal.length (:189-191).
- Named escapes: C_ESCAPES (:155-165) maps all nine of \a \b \t \n \v \f \r \\ \" to the right bytes. That is everything git's quote_c_style emits by name. Other control bytes and DEL come out as 3-digit octal, which the octal branch handles.
- Unquoted input: a path that does not both start and end with `"` returns unchanged (:180). That check is safe because an unquoted header always begins with `b/`, `a/` or `/`. A name containing `"` is always quoted by git, quotePath or not, and decodes through `\"`.
- Prefix order: git's quote_two puts the prefix inside the quotes (`+++ "b/caf\303\251.ts"`). The code unquotes at :249 and only then strips `b/` at :255, which is the correct order.
- /dev/null: git never quotes it, so unquoteGitPath is the identity on it and both comparisons (:245, :250) behave as before.
- No other behaviour change in parseDiff: the only edits are two calls to unquoteGitPath, which is the identity on any header that is not quoted. Every previously correct answer is preserved; only headers that were already broken (quoted ones) change.
- Rename and copy: parseDiff reads no `diff --git`, `rename from`/`rename to` or `copy` lines. A rename with edits still emits `---`/`+++`, which this fix now decodes. A 100% rename emits no `---`/`+++` and contributes nothing, as before. Copy detection needs -C, which is not passed. None of this is changed by the PR.
- Coverage: the tests do cover a multi-byte character (`café`, in both the unit and CLI tests) and a backslash (`back\slash.ts`), plus a tab. Both go through the end-to-end path only, with no direct literal test (see 2).

What a tree read could not establish:
- That CI run 44019198377 ran with default core.quotePath, so that `café` was actually octal-quoted there. I could not see the runner's git config.
- That `bun run check` is green and that the mutation check turns exactly two tests red. Both are taken from the record; I ran nothing.
- How the indexer and discover.ts name a non-UTF-8 file, so whether the U+FFFD output in finding 3 ever reaches a real mismatch.
- On macOS, whether git's NFC form (core.precomposeUnicode) and the filesystem's names that discover.ts reads agree for decomposed names.
finalSummary: Delivered in opum-ai/glyph-cli#62 (commit bd15c53): parseDiff decodes git's C-quoted header path (non-ASCII, backslash and control bytes) to the real UTF-8 path before stripping b/, so symbols in such a file are no longer silently dropped from diff. Validated by CI run 44019198377 on bd15c53 (Check, Docs, Tracker integrity green); bun run check green, 76 tests. Both new tests go red when the unquoting is removed and the other tests in those files stay green.
